title: Respiratory and Psychological Impact of Elective Surgery of Congenital Lung Malformations
official: Respiratory and Psychological Impact of Elective Surgery of Congenital Lung Malformations
summary: The absence of surgery of Congenital lung malformations (CLMs), if it avoids a stressfull event, is accompanied by a "medicalization" of the child, which will be regularly followed up in a specialized medical and surgical environment. The persistent risk of complication, albeit low, is likely to induce over-protective parental behaviours, and to be associated with a sustained family anxiety reaction. The main objective is to test the hypothesis that the absence of surgery has a significant impact on parental anxiety, measurable at 6- 9 years of age.

interventions.name: World Health Organization Quality of Life (WHOQOL-BREF)
Parental Educational Competence Self-Evaluation Questionnaire "Questionnaire d'Auto-Évaluation de la Compétence Éducative Parentale (QAECEP)"

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Child of the MALFPULM cohort, with their parents
* At least one follow-up visit between 0 and 2 years of age (n= 414 eligible children)
* Non-opposition of the family

Exclusion Criteria:

* Child with CLM, but not included in MALFPULM
* Parents who participated in MALPULM, but with prenatal fetal death, or neonatal death.
